subject: Clarifying court access & break-glass carve for FathomTech MSA
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@fathomtech.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Mark Sweeney <mark.sweeney@fathomtech.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FathomTech MSA — governing law & injunctive relief redlines

Karthik —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Attached is a marked MSA (FathomTech_MSA_v2_redline.docx) with the clauses our legal team would like to see clarified on governing law, forum, and emergency relief. High level: we prefer Delaware law and court access for injunctive relief (IP/data safeguards).

Key asks from our side:
- Governing law: Delaware (to match our other vendor contracts)
- Injunctive relief: a clear carve allowing either party to seek equitable relief in court (without forcing arbitration) where necessary for seed data/IP/SSO breaches
- Clarify urgent notice windows and narrow the types of relief that can be sought immediately

We understand Redwood prefers arbitration for most disputes; happy to discuss a limited carve for provisional measures. Can you loop in your contracts/legal so we can agree final language?

Attachment: FathomTech_MSA_v2_redline.docx (docx)

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Legal Ops, FathomTech
elena.ruiz@fathomtech.com
+1 415-555-0128

From: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@fathomtech.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com, Mark Sweeney <mark.sweeney@fathomtech.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FathomTech MSA — governing law & injunctive relief redlines

Elena — thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. Looping in our legal lead (Laura) and contracts (Olga) to align on a pragmatic compromise. Two quick notes from product/legal perspective:

1) We do prefer arbitration as the primary dispute mechanism for speed/cost predictability.
2) We recognize the operational reality that customers sometimes need emergency court orders (injunctions) to protect IP or stop exfiltration of PII. We're open to a narrow provisional-measures carve so long as it:
   - is limited to equitable relief necessary to preserve rights and data;
   - includes notice to Redwood where feasible and a short opportunity to consult;
   - preserves arbitration as the default for all other remedies.

Laura/Olga — can you propose language that:
- keeps arbitration but explicitly preserves either party's right to seek provisional or injunctive relief in court for narrowly-defined categories (IP, data security, law enforcement preservation),
- adds a short emergency-contact SLA and a 72-hour preservation/notice step where practicable, and
- confirms venue (we can accept DE courts for the carve but would like to preserve arbitration seat/location for full disputes).

Proposed next step: Laura/Olga send a tracked-redline back this afternoon and we aim for final by COB tomorrow so ops can spin up onboarding docs.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

From: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@fathomtech.com>
Cc: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FathomTech MSA — governing law & injunctive relief redlines

Elena / Karthik — attached are two items: a short memo (FT-MSA-emergency-relief-notes.pdf) and a tracked-redline we recommend. Summary of our balancing position:

A) Governing law/venue
- We can accept Delaware law for the MSA (substantive law).
- For full dispute resolution, we propose arbitration (seat: New York) as the primary forum to preserve confidentiality and expediency.
- We will include express language that provisional remedies (injunctive relief) may be sought in state or federal court in Delaware (for preservation of rights) without waiving arbitration.

B) Injunctive/provisional measures carve (draft language highlights)
- "Notwithstanding the agreement to arbitrate, either party may seek equitable relief, including injunctive or other provisional remedies, in any court of competent jurisdiction to prevent irreparable harm concerning intellectual property rights, protection of customer data, or immediate security incidents."
- Add a clause requiring prompt notice to Redwood with a 48–72 hour remediation consultation window where practicable, unless exigent circumstances make notice impracticable.

C) Practical operational items
- Emergency contact for FathomTech (name/phone/email) to be included in the order form.
- Redwood will commit to a 24-hour acknowledgement SLA and an internal 72-hour triage timeline for suspected PII breaches tied to escalation steps.

D) Why this works: it preserves arbitration for commercial claims, gives FathomTech immediate court options when necessary for IP/data stops, and creates an operational path to de-escalate before broad litigation/arbitration.

Olga will circulate the redline (minor wording tweaks on notice windows). If FathomTech accepts the carve and the venue split (DE law; NY arbitration seat) we can finalize language for signatures.

Attachment: FT-MSA-emergency-relief-notes.pdf (pdf)

Regards,
Laura Bennett
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@fathomtech.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Mark Sweeney <mark.sweeney@fathomtech.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FathomTech MSA — governing law & injunctive relief redlines

Laura — thanks, this is helpful and much closer to what we need. Two small points from our side:
1) Can we tighten the notice language so it's "where feasible, at least 48 hours' notice" (we have internal approval gates that need a short window for review)?
2) For the arbitration seat, would Redwood accept New York or Delaware? NY is fine for us if agreed.

If you can incorporate those tweaks I can take a final look and mark 'approved' for our legal director. If both firms agree, let's target signature next week.

Thanks again —
Elena
